Senses.Explanation: To take something up as one's own is to accept and stand under a presented saying, claim, capacity, or matter so that it can be used or answered for. Yuanwu Keqin joins taking it up directly with using it and acting when needed. Tianru Weize locates the matter in each listener's own share and asks for direct personal uptake; Baichi Xingyuan similarly links immediate uptake with recognizing one's own ground. Pu'an Yinsu faults people who will not take up the awakening manifest before their eyes. The same verb can expose a premature or inadequate stopping place. Hongzhi Zhengjue says one must exhaust the subtle before understanding the matter of taking-up; Micang Daokai ridicules defensive calculation about it, and Dawei Jinglun contrasts what follows a phrase with the move before the mechanism, then rebukes being caught on either side. In Xuefeng Huikong's verse, ‘Dazhi’ is Baizhang Huaihai, the titled case figure who takes it up and is deaf for three days.

Senses.Explanation: Receiving emptiness and answering an echo is responding to what has no substance of one’s own. Chan speakers apply the paired image to inherited talk and imitative responses, often immediately contrasting it with a present demand or blow. Yinyuan Longqi contrasts empty reception with working the local ground; Chaozong applies it to inherited talk; Tianyin Xiu warns the echo-following person not to move; Baiyu Jingsi applies the phrase to Kasyapa in the flower-sermon case; and Lianyue forbids it while raising the whisk.

Senses.Explanation: The idiom of secondhand realization — riding the empty, catching echoes — the masters' charge against heirs who take the hollow of the ancestors' words and pass on only the sound, from the Song halls to the Qing. Mi'an Xianjie, at the Wuju mountain hall, sweeps the whole apparatus away — wedge driven out by wedge turns into ruts, mind transmitted by mind deepens the sickness, Bodhidharma missed the head-on word and faced the wall nine years — and the descendants after him ride the empty and catch echoes: raised brows and blinking eyes, staff-work and shout-work, all leaves stopping a baby's cry, while Wuju goes straight up with no road to heaven and no door into earth, teeth clenched, kneading mud and water with them until the staff falls: without one bout of bone-piercing cold, how could the plum blossom scent the nose; Dahui Zonggao, eulogizing two Chan men at their stupa, walks the seal down the line — Baiyun sold it cheap to the board-carrying man, Wuzu pasted it over with three pounds of hemp, Yuanwu his teacher scattered all three hundred sixty bones and eighty-four thousand pores into the assembly's laps — then draws a border with the staff that may not be crossed, and breaks the seal before them all so the descendants each get a livelihood of their own, spared riding the empty and catching echoes and dulling one another down the line; eyelashes and brows all fallen and the onlookers laugh without end; Zhongfeng Mingben works Xiangyan's enlightenment verse line by line — one strike and all knowing forgotten, the nod and the ancient road, no trace anywhere, dignity beyond sound and sight — then rules the men everywhere who claim the Way: which of them truly says the uppermost vehicle? They ride the empty and catch echoes; hence what covers heaven and earth must flow out of your own chest, and next to it the seers-and-hearers school-solutions count ten against a hundred; Tianyin Yuanxiu raises Shitou and Yaoshan — words and deeds no concern, not-words and not-deeds no concern either, a needle will not enter here, flowers planted on stone — grants the two elders the stringless zither and its birthless song, father and son squared; yet the family shame shows to bystanders, and the man who rides the empty and catches echoes had best not touch it: touch it, thirty blows. Yinyuan Longqi spends the idiom on the carriers themselves — the great clamor Bodhidharma carried east to this soil; riding the empty and catching echoes, the Sixth Patriarch hauled it over the Lingnan ranges; they thought the ferrying of beings done, and how many monks are still unwilling — so Huangbo breaks the clods where it stands, levels the high and fills the low, lifts when it lifts, releases when it releases; Tian'an Sheng, run through the maze of delusion and awakening at the Qingzhou hall — how many trip on flat ground, watching the moon above and losing the oar in hand — and when the monk, three bows in, answers much-obliged for the master's instruction, gets back two words: a man riding the empty and catching echoes; then the said-or-not-said turned once more — to speak is surplus, not to speak is dulling; if spoken, what has been spoken; if not, what are the teeth chattering now; Yulin Tongxiu takes up Xuefeng as rice-cook under Deshan — bell not yet rung, drum not yet beaten, where does the old man carry his bowl? — big Deshan never got the last word, and next day, the master risen different from usual, Yantou claps and laughs: glad the old man has it, none under heaven can touch him, and even so only three years to live — and Yulin rules the echo-catcher glosses over Deshan while the strength-or-weakness bender buries Yantou: the mountain monk reports it straight to the schools, teacher strong and heir strong, give it back to the Deshan father and son; and Yunwai Xingze holds up the Diamond Sutra at the Qizhou Bodhi hall — one raw-iron spine of a World-Honored One standing ten thousand fathoms, barely knocked by Subhuti and rolling off into the grass — yet a man who enters the water knows the tall one: had the sutra stopped at thus-abide and thus-subdue, where would today's echo-riding men grope for it? The mountain monk is otherwise — hearing willing indeed, World-Honored One, joyful to hear — pierced straight through.

Senses.Explanation: Follow the words and you lose it; cling to the phrase and you are deluded. A warning against taking verbal form as the living point of a teaching. Current deployments include Feiyin Tongrong in J26nB178, Tian'an Sheng in J26nB187, Sanyi Mingyu in J27nB189, Baiyu Jingsi in J36nB359, and Yikui Yuankui in J37nB388. The full paired image remains the lexical unit. The current uses still speak and explain; they caution against fixation, not language itself.

Senses.Explanation: On whose grace and power is the standing question masters put to an assembly at the moment a benefit has just been tallied — grain eaten from the year's harvest, a new bell hung, a hall rebuilt by donors, a mind that does all that is needed. Hongzhi Zhengjue closes his address for the departing monastery steward with it, an unnamed monk opens Consort Wang's lecture with it, and Yuanwu Keqin presses it again at an inner-palace lecture. Dahui Zonggao plants it inside a letter as a resting place for investigation, Tianru Weize sets it at the end of a written instruction, and Xutang Zhiyu, Xisou Shaotan, and Zhufeng Zhenxu raise it over new bells, harvest stores, and a Buddha's-birthday rebuilding. At the harvest-steward addresses the question follows an inventory of what the monastery has received. Hongzhi Zhengjue recites the year of muddy farming, the grain pounded at the mill, the fragrant rice shared from a thousand bowls, asks what fills the belly — chan or rice — and ends his verse after the quoted Yaoshan line with the question and flails striking from all four sides. Xutang Zhiyu counts the great vessel of a thousand jun already raised to the tower and ten thousand hu of pearl-grain already stored, the monks entering the hall bellied and spreading their bowls, and asks it before striking his staff. Xisou Shaotan follows one grain from before the division of yin and yang to the singing walk after the meal, and asks it with a shout. At palace lectures and donor occasions the question faces the throne and the benefactors. An unnamed monk asks Consort Wang's assembled lecture — sky covering all, earth bearing the mountains and rivers — at just this moment, on whose grace and power; Yuanwu Keqin answers with one spring blossom amid a thousand flowers and adds that one must also know this grace. At an inner-palace lecture Yuanwu Keqin carries a single phrase out of the crown of a thousand sages through the whole of space as one great gate of liberation, then asks the assembly the question and answers it with the formless Buddha on the mountain of the five aggregates, lighting and shaking the sands. On the Buddha's birthday Zhufeng Zhenxu asks the question over a rebuilt seven-tiered lantern display and answers it himself: by the grace of the grand defender and the civil and military officials who gladly donated their salaries, the donors all sharing in a cause that does not wear away. In written instruction the question becomes the thread of the work itself. Dahui Zonggao tells Zhang the judicial commissioner that when all that needed doing is done, everything follows the mind with nothing lacking — just at that moment, on whose grace and power — and to keep working like this day upon day, like a man learning to shoot who naturally hits. Tianru Weize tells the trainee Zhao to set the inherited tangles aside and press hard on the one thing under investigation in every place and time — in the end, on whose grace and power. The question also opened bell ceremonies and travelled in re-edited letters. Tian'an Sheng gives the new bell its voice — no wings, yet its sound reaches the nine heavens — and asks the question over the red furnace where everything turns into a dance. The same Dahui letter that plants the question in the reply to Zhang also circulated under the title of an instruction to Zhang, the re-edition reading 'just at this moment' where the reply reads 'at this moment.'

Senses.Explanation: The great intent of the coming from the west. Xueqiao Yuanxin tells a donor-feast assembly that coughing, spitting, swinging the arms — all of it is the ancestor's westward intent, needing only one who truly trusts it, Yunwai Xingze tells trainees who came to fathom it that they are already wrong, for he has sat at their crown-door for measureless kalpas, closer than seeking, and Guxue Zhenzhe sings it wholly clear in a spring verse where flowers bud and trees sprout. Senses.Explanation: The “meaning from the West” is the shortened public-interview form of the question about the patriarch’s coming from the West; the records answer it with fresh words and actions rather than one explanatory definition. Direct abbreviated questions ask simply “what is the meaning from the West?” Tianzhu Chonghui answers with a white ape carrying its young and butterflies holding flowers; Helin Xuansu answers that understanding is not understanding and doubt is not doubt. Yunfeng Zudeng answers with striking the forehead and nose, an unnamed monk asks Mazu Daoyi and Mazu answers “what meaning is present now?”, Sanfeng Hanyue Fazang says “three years carrying one boat,” Longya asks Linji and Linji demands the Chan board, Zhaozhou descends from the seat, and Shitou sends the questioner to ask the exposed pillar. The Chan bend is the abbreviation’s life as a public test whose many incompatible replies are preserved rather than harmonized into a hidden proposition.

Yunmen Wenyan sets the frame at his address to the assembly — sun and moon shine slantwise on three continents and straight on four — then, saying he has it glossed for them, demands the sentence, and answers in their stead: eastern continent... western continent; Wuzu Fayan, styling himself the White Cloud elder, raises his hand and makes a Buddha of the whole apparatus — the twenty-eight heavens for a head, the golden wheel's waters for feet, the four continents for a body — then makes a second model: each continent a Buddha, grass and trees a Buddha, all moving and breathing a Buddha — and hands each thing back to itself, dharmas abiding in their positions, the world's marks ever present; Yuanwu Keqin shrinks the great square beyond-outside into a millet grain and the whole void into a palm-leaf, drags Silla and Champa to butt heads, and shoots: arrow loosed in the eastern body-continent, target struck in Aparagodaniya; and Linquan Conglun, appraising the case of hiding in the Dipper, simply glosses the geography — four continents on Sumeru's four faces, east, south, west, north, these the Sanskrit sounds — then asks where the Dipper hides its body, knocking the forehead in vain, searching in vain. Sanyi Mingyu presses the one-body question at general discourse — everywhere is one thing only, so why does this southern continent not know the northern continent's business, the eastern Poverty-goddess land not know Aparagodaniya's, the lower floors not know the Joy heavens? — then whisks raised, kneads the four continents into one lump, east and west indistinguishable, the western meaning the eastern meaning; Qianshan Shengren Hanke, seeing the Zhao brothers' family off to a new temple in Liaoyang, works the farewell verse through the borrowed map — gate and hall crossing places, pillars and lanterns swapping seats, the northern continent ringing its bell, Aparagodaniya's dogs barking, Indra's palace shaken, the eastern sea's carp at boil — and still the waves calm, the green hills and waters as before; Shitian Faxun spends eight graphs at the hall address — eastern continent, western continent; clear clear water, the swimming fish themselves lost; and Yulin Tongxiu, closing the retreat, runs the whole tour — sitting cross-legged in the southern continent, legs gone numb in the northern, bowl in hand in the eastern, arms aching in the western — then turns over on the ocean floor, knocks down Tushita's palace, tweaks the nose of old Yama until the four great kings sneeze in chorus, and warns: failing that, grass the moment you step out the door — mind your feet.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 不空過，山河大地．草木叢林．情與無情悉不空過，至於拄杖子亦不空過。拄杖子既不空過，且道成得箇什麼？通身黑漆麤刺梨，非但登山兼打狗。冬夜，小參。過去諸佛關空鎻夢，見在諸佛寄帽投河，未來諸佛望梅止渴。大眾！古今日月．古今山河．古今人倫．古今節令，汝等諸人各各含齒帶髮，第一莫受人瞞。如今有般漢，纔聞輕輕舉著，便向這裏取次承當，一向定將去、合將去，要且只知仲冬嚴寒、孟夏漸熱，殊不知孟夏漸熱、仲冬嚴寒。乳峯恁麼告報，且道是瞞人自瞞？為復別有長處？良久，云：傾心吐膽無人會，拔舌犁耕只自知。解制，小參。拈拄杖示眾，云：看，看！十方世界，若凡、若聖．情與無情，盡向這裏安居，結制一夏九十日，今日告終。其中所得法門、所修行願各各不同，所謂諸佛則具足一切種智，其諸菩薩則成就波羅蜜門，自餘有學、無學，這一隊不唧𠺕漢置而勿論。只如見前一眾與山僧於此眉毛𤺊結一夏，牙齒敲磕，且道還有所得也無？若有所得，埋沒大眾；若無所得，辜負山僧。正與麼時如何？卓一下，云：西風一陣來，落葉兩三片。結制，小參。坐斷主人翁，不落第二見，一念萬年，萬年一念，便恁麼去，百二十日夏未是長期。其或未然，鄮峯別有箇方便，窮則變，變則通，盞子撲落地，楪子成七八片。卓拄杖一下。解夏，小參。百二十日夏，如今已告圓，就中一句子，切忌錯流傳。眾中莫有通方底？出來將錯就錯道一句看。若也道得，後園驢喫草；若道不得，秋至鴈㗸蘆。冬夜，小參。六爻既窮，陰魔自殄；一陽來復，吾道大亨。洞山菓子格外安排，皓老布裩依前赫赤，鄮峯寡不敵眾，相逢相見隨例道箇仲冬嚴寒，且要諸人順時保愛。若據從頭數來，灼然大有事在。何故？九九八十一，窮漢受罪畢，方始展脚眠，蚊虫獦蚤出。救攝，急急。結夏，小參。風恬浪靜，切忌嚲跟；白日青天，宜須退步。鄮峯放一線道：且與諸人恁麼商量。忽然結却布袋頭，直得山河大地變作山河大地、吞却山河大地，你衲僧家畢竟向甚處出氣？拍禪床，云：無人知此意，令我憶南泉。解夏，小參。面門一思，長時無間，見成句子，百味完全。若論結也，當處安居，不是拽短就長；至於解也，隨方任運，亦非拽長就短。黃連甜，甘草苦，擲地金聲如糞土，睦州拶折雲門脚，南泉不打鹽官鼓。卓拄杖一下。冬夜，小參。諸佛不出世，祖師不西來，顢頇一句子，南嶽對天台。靈利漢不在商量，性燥底何勞重舉？只
